findings.title: "Silence notifications" menu item is shown but does nothing in the new rule list
findings.body: In the new list view, GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule (the `rule` prop is undefined). AlertRuleMenu now derives the Silence ability from the Prometheus rule via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the "Silence notifications" menu item renders enabled and clicking it calls handleSilence -> setShowSilenceDrawer(true). However, the drawer is gated on `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>}`; with `rule` undefined the drawer never mounts, so clicking the menu item is a silent no-op. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts that the Silence menu item exists, never that clicking it opens anything. The silence flow needs to be driven from the prom rule/identifier, or the item should be hidden when no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: Delete and Pause actions no longer appear in the list view rule menu
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu gates the Delete item on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). The new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons.V2) never passes a rulerRule, only a GrafanaPromRuleDTO, so even though canDelete/canPause can now be satisfied through useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, the Delete and Pause items never render. Previously the list passed the ruler rule and both actions were available. The updated GrafanaGroupLoader test codifies the regression by asserting exactly 4 menu items (silence, duplicate, copy link, export) with no delete. Users of the new list view can no longer delete or pause rules from it, which is a functional regression beyond the stated goal of removing ruler API requests.

findings.title: Federated rule groups lose their edit/delete immutability protection
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities (which backs useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities used across the old list view and detail views) previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated rules as immutable, hiding Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently. This PR rewrites it to delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. As a result, for Mimir/GEM federated (cross-tenant, source_tenants) rule groups, those actions now report as supported whenever permissions allow, rendering Edit/Delete/Pause buttons that were previously suppressed; attempted operations will fail at the ruler API or mutate a group the UI previously treated as read-only.

findings.title: Duplicate menu item becomes enabled for data-source rules based on Grafana-internal create permission
findings.body: canDuplicate now ORs the ruler-based ability with the result of useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. For a non-Grafana (Mimir/Cortex/Loki) rule, promRule fails prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule so skipToken is passed, producing useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). With rule undefined, loading=false makes duplicateSupported=true, and the allowed side is checked against getRulesPermissions('grafana').create (alert.rules:create). A user who has Grafana-managed rule create permission but lacks alert.rules.external:write will now see the "Duplicate" menu item on cloud rules; before this change only the ruler-based ability (which requires the external write permission) was consulted. The backend still enforces permissions, but the UI now advertises an action the user cannot complete.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key in the filtered rule list
findings.body: In the rules.map switch, the 'grafana' branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={...} .../>` without `key={key}`; the replaced GrafanaRuleLoader had key={key}, and the sibling 'datasource' and 'default' branches still pass key. React will emit a missing-key warning, and mixing keyed and unkeyed siblings in the same list can cause React to mis-associate per-item component state (e.g. RuleActionsButtons' silence drawer / delete modal state) when the list updates.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules lose the Export menu item in the list view
findings.body: The new prom-based ability gates ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) (`[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]`), whereas the ruler-based path used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), which also matches recording rules. In the new list view only the prom-based path runs (no rulerRule is fetched), so Grafana-managed recording rules no longer show the "Export / With modifications" menu entry even though they did before and modify-export is valid for recording rules.

findings.title: Rule view link drops the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem (in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail page returned the user to the filtered list. The new component uses createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) with no returnTo, breaking return-to-previous navigation for rules opened from the new list and filter views.

findings.title: JSDoc still claims the group is loaded from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints
findings.body: The comment above GrafanaGroupLoader says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints", but this PR removed the ruler query (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery) — only the Prometheus endpoint is queried now. The expectedRulesCount prop comment also still references the ruler response. These stale comments misdescribe the component's behavior after the change.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name referring to ruler rule preloading
findings.body: After removing the alertRuleApi getGrafanaRulerGroup prefetch, the comment "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX..." and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` are stale — the block now only upserts the Prometheus groups cache. The comment should be updated so readers don't think ruler preloading still happens here.
